cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, has finished building the house of the LORD (1 Kings 6:14). Now he stands before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel. Then he spreads out his hands toward heaven.

cards.question: Solomon is standing at the altar with his hands spread toward heaven, and all Israel is watching. What does he do?

answers.text: He prays to the LORD
He reads from the law
He sings a song of David

cards.text: Solomon opens with "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below…" No warm-up, no small talk, he goes straight to the TOP.

cards.question: Solomon says God keeps His covenant of loving devotion with His servants. Which servants?

answers.text: Those who walk before Him with all their hearts
Those who bring Him the most offerings
Those who were born in Jerusalem

cards.text: Then Solomon brings up his father, King David.

cards.question: Solomon says God is still waiting to keep His promise to his father David.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: In Solomon's words, what God spoke with His mouth, He fulfilled with His hand. Friend, I've promised to scrub the ovens about four hundred times, and I've actually done it maybe TWO.
Now Solomon asks God to keep what He promised David about the throne of Israel.

cards.question: What did God promise David about the throne of Israel?

answers.text: David would never fail to have a man on it
It would move to a bigger city
Solomon would sit on it forever

cards.question: God's promise about the throne came with a condition: David's descendants had to walk before Him as David did.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Solomon asks God to confirm His promise to David. Then he stops and asks a big question: "But will God indeed dwell upon the earth?"

cards.question: Solomon just built God a temple. What does he say about God and that temple?

answers.text: It can't contain God and neither can heaven
God will now live only inside it
It's grand enough to hold all of God

cards.text: Even so, Solomon asks God to regard the prayer he's praying today. He asks God's eyes to be open toward this temple night and day, the place about which God said "My Name shall be there".

cards.question: Solomon asks God to keep His eyes open toward the temple. Why?

answers.text: So He'll hear prayers prayed toward it
So He'll guard it from enemies
So He'll watch over the priests

cards.text: Whenever Solomon and the people of Israel pray toward this place, he asks God to hear them.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to hear His people's prayers from ___, His dwelling place.

answers.text: heaven
Zion
the temple

cards.question: Solomon asks God to hear His people's prayers and also to forgive them.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Now Solomon walks through one situation after another. First: when a man sins against his neighbor and has to take an oath, he comes before the altar in the temple.

cards.question: A man has sinned against his neighbor and takes an oath at the altar. What does Solomon ask God to do from heaven?

answers.text: Condemn the wicked and justify the righteous
Forgive them both and send them home
Let the priests settle the whole matter

cards.text: Next situation: when Israel is defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against God. The temple's brand new, and Solomon's already planning for the bad days, like me reading the warranty on a new oven before I even plug it IN.

cards.question: Israel has just been defeated because of their sin. What does Solomon picture them doing next?

answers.text: Returning to God and praying in the temple
Gathering a bigger army to fight again
Leaving the land to start over somewhere

cards.text: Then Solomon asks God to hear from heaven and forgive the sin of His people.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to give His defeated people a new land to live in.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Next situation: when the skies are shut and there's no rain because the people have sinned against God. The sky just closes up shop, friend, like a bakery with the lights off and the sign flipped to CLOSED.

cards.question: With no rain, the people pray toward the temple. They ___ God's name and ___ from their sins.

answers.text: confess
turn
forget
hide
curse

cards.text: Solomon asks God to hear from heaven, forgive His people, and send rain on the land. Forgiveness AND rain, friend: that's not one cookie, that's the whole BOX.

cards.question: Solomon wants God to forgive His people and send rain. What else does he want God to do for them?

answers.text: Teach them the good way to walk
Give them a brand new law
Make them the richest nation

cards.text: Then Solomon names trouble that may come: famine, plague, blight, mildew, locusts, grasshoppers, and enemies besieging their cities. Locusts AND grasshoppers, friend, this man is not leaving ONE bug off the list.
Whatever the trouble, each one knows his own afflictions and spreads out his hands toward the temple.

cards.question: Someone in trouble spreads out his hands toward the temple, and Solomon asks God to forgive and act. How does he ask God to repay each man?

answers.text: According to all his ways
According to what the priests decide
According to the size of his offering

cards.question: Solomon says only God knows the hearts of all people.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Solomon wants the people to fear God all the days they live in the land. Then he turns to someone who isn't from Israel at all, and friend, I did NOT see it coming: a foreigner who has come from a distant land because of God's name.

cards.question: A foreigner comes from far away and prays toward the temple. What does Solomon ask God to do?

answers.text: Do all the foreigner asks Him
Send him back to his own land
Have him go through a priest

cards.question: If God answers the foreigner's prayer, what does Solomon say will happen?

answers.text: All peoples will know God's name
The foreigner will move to Jerusalem
Israel will grow richer and stronger

cards.text: Next: when Israel goes to war wherever God sends them, they pray toward the city God chose and the house Solomon built for His Name.

cards.question: In Solomon's prayer, Israel is out at war, praying toward the city God chose. What does Solomon ask God to do?

answers.text: Hear them and uphold their cause
Bring them home before the fight
Keep the temple safe while they're gone

cards.text: Then Solomon says it plainly: "there is no one who does not sin…" Not the king, not the priests, and DEFINITELY not a stamper who keeps "taste-testing" the chocolate chips.

cards.question: In Solomon's prayer, Israel sins and God becomes angry with them. What does Solomon picture happening?

answers.text: An enemy takes them captive to his land
The temple falls down to the ground
Their king is driven from the throne

cards.question: Solomon pictures captive Israel, in an enemy's land, coming to their senses and admitting they have sinned and done wrong.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: In Solomon's prayer, the captives in the enemy's land return to God. How do they return to Him?

answers.text: With all their heart and soul
With gifts for the temple
With a new king to lead them

cards.text: Solomon asks God to hear their prayer from heaven, uphold their cause, and forgive all they've done against Him.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to grant the captives ___ in the eyes of their captors, so they'd be shown mercy.

answers.text: compassion
strength
riches

cards.question: Solomon gives God a reason to show His captive people mercy. What is it?

answers.text: They're His people and His inheritance
They built Him a beautiful temple
They've suffered long enough already

cards.text: God brought them out of Egypt, which Solomon calls "the furnace for iron". I stand next to ovens all day, friend, and even I don't want to go anywhere called THAT.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to listen to His people only when they pray inside the temple.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: One more reason: God set Israel apart from all the peoples of the earth as His inheritance. He said so back when He brought their fathers out of Egypt.

cards.question: God said He was setting Israel apart when He brought them out of Egypt. Which servant did He speak through?

answers.text: Moses
Samuel
David

cards.text: That's Moses, Israel's leader, and that's where Solomon's prayer ends. But stick around, friend, because this temple's story is far from done.
